paper.title: A contribution to the mathematical theory of epidemics (SIS variant; endemic threshold)

headline: SIS endemic threshold (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; prevalence(R0=0.8)=0.0000, prevalence(R0=2.0)=0.4761 (i*=0.5)

verdicts.gate: P1 endemic threshold at R0=1 (prevalence<0.02 at R0=0.8 AND >0.3 at R0=2.0)
P2 endemic prevalence within +/-0.05 of i*=1-1/R0 at R0 in [1.5, 2.0, 3.0]
P3 prevalence monotone non-decreasing in R0; <0.02 at R0=0.8

extra.i_star_formula: i* = 1 - 1/R0 (R0>1), evaluated at the LOCKED R0
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the SIS endemic threshold + i*=1-1/R0 and would catch an artifact

citations: Kermack, W.O. & McKendrick, A.G. (1927). A contribution to the mathematical theory of epidemics. Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 115(772):700-721. doi:10.1098/rspa.1927.0118.
Hethcote, H.W. (2000). The Mathematics of Infectious Diseases. SIAM Review 42(4):599-653. doi:10.1137/S0036144500371907. (Standard SIS endemic equilibrium i* = 1 - 1/R0.)
Anderson, R.M. & May, R.M. (1991). Infectious Diseases of Humans: Dynamics and Control. Oxford University Press.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction; the analytic i*=1-1/R0 is the comparison anchor
